name: Cardiovex

content.label: treated patients still have uncontrolled blood pressure on three or more medicines

blocks.talking_point: About one in five treated patients remain above target despite three or more antihypertensives. Excess aldosterone is a common driver.
facts: Roughly 1 in 5 patients treated for hypertension remain uncontrolled on three or more antihypertensive medicines.
Excess aldosterone is a common driver of resistant hypertension.

content.title: What is Cardiovex?
content.text: A once-daily oral aldosterone synthase inhibitor.
bullets: Add-on therapy for adults with resistant hypertension

blocks.talking_point: Cardiovex is a once-daily oral aldosterone synthase inhibitor, used as add-on therapy for adults with resistant hypertension.
facts: Cardiovex is a once-daily oral aldosterone synthase inhibitor.
Cardiovex is indicated as add-on therapy for adults with resistant hypertension, meaning blood pressure uncontrolled on three or more antihypertensives including a diuretic.
Cardiovex is not indicated for children or for use in pregnancy.

steps.title: Inhibit
steps.text: Cardiovex blocks aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2) in the adrenal gland

steps.title: Reduce
steps.text: Less aldosterone is produced, so the kidney retains less sodium and water

steps.title: Lower
steps.text: Blood volume falls and blood pressure comes down

blocks.talking_point: Cardiovex blocks aldosterone synthase in the adrenal gland. Less aldosterone means less sodium and water retention, so blood pressure falls.
facts: Cardiovex inhibits aldosterone synthase, the enzyme CYP11B2, in the adrenal gland.
Lower aldosterone reduces sodium and water retention by the kidney, which lowers blood volume and blood pressure.
Unlike mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, which block the aldosterone receptor, Cardiovex reduces aldosterone production itself.

content.title: Selective by design
content.text: Targets aldosterone synthesis while leaving cortisol synthesis alone.
bullets: No change in cortisol levels versus placebo in ASCEND-HTN

blocks.talking_point: It is selective for aldosterone synthase, and cortisol levels were unchanged versus placebo in the pivotal trial.
facts: Cardiovex is selective for aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2) over the cortisol-producing enzyme CYP11B1.
In ASCEND-HTN, cortisol levels did not differ between Cardiovex and placebo.

content.title: Change in systolic blood pressure at week 12

blocks.talking_point: Systolic pressure fell 15.2 millimetres of mercury on Cardiovex versus 5.1 on placebo at week 12, a difference of about 10.
facts: Primary endpoint: mean change in seated systolic blood pressure at week 12 was -15.2 mmHg with Cardiovex versus -5.1 mmHg with placebo.
The placebo-adjusted difference was -10.1 mmHg, p < 0.001.
Blood pressure reductions were seen from week 2 onward.

content.label: reached target blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg

blocks.talking_point: Nearly half of patients, 48 percent, reached target below 130 over 80, compared with 21 percent on placebo.
facts: At week 12, 48% of patients on Cardiovex reached blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg versus 21% on placebo.

blocks.talking_point: ASCEND-HTN was a phase 3 randomised double-blind trial in 812 adults already on three or more antihypertensives.
facts: ASCEND-HTN was a phase 3, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
It enrolled 812 adults with resistant hypertension on three or more antihypertensives including a diuretic.
Treatment lasted 12 weeks. Longer-term outcome data are not yet available.

content.footnote: Events reported in 3% or more of patients on Cardiovex.

blocks.talking_point: Most adverse events were close to placebo. Headache was the most common. Hyperkalaemia was more frequent on Cardiovex, 3.9 versus 1.2 percent.
facts: Headache: 6.1% with Cardiovex versus 5.4% with placebo.
Dizziness: 4.8% versus 3.1%.
Hyperkalaemia: 3.9% versus 1.2%.
Fatigue: 3.2% versus 2.9%.
No cases of adrenal insufficiency were reported in ASCEND-HTN.

blocks.talking_point: Discontinuation due to adverse events was low, 2.3 percent versus 1.9 on placebo.
facts: Discontinuation due to adverse events: 2.3% with Cardiovex versus 1.9% with placebo.

content.title: Monitoring
content.text: Check serum potassium and renal function.
bullets: Before starting, at week 2, then periodically
Not recommended if potassium is above 5.0 mmol/L or eGFR is below 30

blocks.talking_point: Check potassium and renal function before starting, at week two and periodically. It is not recommended with potassium above 5 or eGFR below 30.
facts: Check serum potassium and renal function before starting Cardiovex, at week 2, and periodically thereafter.
Cardiovex is not recommended in patients with serum potassium above 5.0 mmol/L or eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m2.
Use caution with potassium supplements and potassium-sparing diuretics.

steps.title: Week 4
steps.text: Increase to 20 mg once daily if blood pressure is still above target

blocks.talking_point: Start at 10 milligrams once daily, check potassium at week two, and increase to 20 milligrams at week four if pressure is still above target.
facts: Starting dose is 10 mg orally once daily.
Check serum potassium at week 2.
The dose may be increased to 20 mg once daily at week 4 if blood pressure remains above target.
The maximum dose is 20 mg once daily.

content.title: Practical points
bullets: Missed dose: skip it, do not double up
No adjustment in mild to moderate hepatic impairment

blocks.talking_point: It can be taken with or without food. A missed dose is skipped, not doubled. No adjustment is needed in mild to moderate hepatic impairment.
facts: Cardiovex can be taken with or without food, at the same time each day.
If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the usual time. Do not double the dose.
No dose adjustment is needed in mild to moderate hepatic impairment. It has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment.
Continue the patient's existing antihypertensive medicines.

slides.title: Who it is for, and key takeaways
slides.subtitle: Summary

content.title: The right patient
bullets: Uncontrolled on 3 or more agents including a diuretic

blocks.talking_point: The right patient is an adult still uncontrolled on three or more agents including a diuretic, with eGFR of at least 30 and potassium no higher than 5.
facts: Appropriate patients are adults with blood pressure uncontrolled on three or more antihypertensives including a diuretic.
Patients should have eGFR of 30 mL/min/1.73m2 or above and serum potassium of 5.0 mmol/L or below.

content.title: Key takeaways
bullets: 10.1 mmHg greater systolic reduction than placebo

blocks.talking_point: Three takeaways: about 10 millimetres greater systolic reduction than placebo, nearly half of patients at target by week 12, and once-daily dosing with potassium monitoring.
facts: Cardiovex gave a 10.1 mmHg greater reduction in systolic blood pressure than placebo at week 12.
48% of patients reached target blood pressure by week 12.
Dosing is once daily, with potassium monitoring.
